meta.name: Microsoft Identity and Access Administrator (SC-300)
meta.notes: Initial pack: 10 questions covering Microsoft Entra ID administration — external identities (B2B), Conditional Access, phishing-resistant authentication, Identity Protection, Privileged Identity Management, Access Reviews, app registrations, hybrid identity, managed identities, and Entitlement Management. Authored 2026-06-06 [scheduled-agent].

questions.question: A multinational firm collaborates with external auditors who need temporary access to a SharePoint Online site. Which Microsoft Entra capability lets you invite the auditors using their existing work email, federate authentication back to their home tenants, and recertify or revoke their access on a schedule?
options: Microsoft Entra External ID (B2B collaboration) with Access Reviews applied to the guest accounts
Microsoft Entra External ID for customers (B2C) with custom user flows for the auditors
Active Directory Federation Services trusts established with each auditor's tenant
Cloud-only member accounts created in the home tenant and shared with the auditors
questions.explanation: Entra External ID B2B collaboration invites external users as guest objects in your tenant; they sign in against their home tenant and you control access via groups, Conditional Access, and Access Reviews that can auto-deny on no response. Entra External ID for customers (B2C) is for consumer-facing apps and uses a separate customer tenant — wrong audience. AD FS federation trusts require owning and operating the federation; standing up one per vendor is impractical. Creating member accounts gives external auditors tenant-wide entitlements (and Entra licence consumption) while bypassing every collaboration safeguard.

questions.question: You must require multifactor authentication for users signing in to any Microsoft 365 cloud app from anywhere except the corporate office IP ranges, using the smallest number of Conditional Access policies. Which configuration meets the requirement?
options: Two policies: one grants access from the trusted named location, and a second requires MFA for every other sign-in
One policy targeting all users and all cloud apps, requiring MFA as the grant control, with the trusted named location excluded from the policy assignment
Enable security defaults at the tenant level and register the office IP ranges as trusted networks in the multifactor authentication service settings
One policy that blocks sign-ins from any location not listed as named, plus a second policy that requires MFA from the trusted locations
questions.explanation: A single Conditional Access policy scoped to all users and all cloud apps, with the trusted named (IP) location excluded under Conditions → Locations and MFA chosen as the grant control, expresses the requirement in one rule. Splitting into two grant policies is redundant. Security defaults cannot be scoped by location and enforce MFA on every user — and they cannot coexist with Conditional Access. Blocking unknown locations while requiring MFA from trusted ones inverts the intent.

questions.question: Your security team wants to eliminate passwords for staff who sign in from shared lab kiosks. The method must be phishing-resistant, and the kiosks have no enrolled mobile phone. Which authentication method should you enable in the Authentication methods policy?
options: SMS one-time passcodes delivered to a desk phone shared by the lab team
Microsoft Authenticator push notifications with number matching enabled
FIDO2 security keys, registered per user in the Authentication methods policy
Windows Hello for Business with a shared kiosk PIN configured at first sign-in
questions.explanation: FIDO2 security keys are phishing-resistant (the WebAuthn protocol binds the credential to the origin), need no mobile phone, and are explicitly supported for shared/kiosk scenarios in Entra. SMS is not phishing-resistant and is being deprecated as a primary factor. Microsoft Authenticator requires the user's mobile device — excluded by the scenario. Windows Hello for Business is per-user, TPM-bound, and is not designed to be shared across users on a kiosk.

questions.question: You enable a sign-in risk policy in Microsoft Entra ID Protection that requires MFA when the risk level is medium or high. A user calls the helpdesk complaining about repeated MFA challenges after travelling abroad. Where is the authoritative place to investigate, confirm compromise or dismiss the detections for that account?
options: Microsoft Defender for Cloud Apps activity log under app governance
Microsoft Sentinel incidents queue filtered to the user principal name
Entra ID Protection's Risky users and Risky sign-ins reports
Microsoft Purview Insider Risk Management alerts queue
questions.explanation: Entra ID Protection's Risky users and Risky sign-ins blades are the source of truth for risk detections (atypical travel, leaked credentials, anonymous IP, malware-linked IP, etc.) — and they expose the Confirm compromised / Confirm safe / Dismiss actions. Defender for Cloud Apps covers SaaS app and session risk, not Entra identity risk state. Sentinel can ingest Entra signals but its incident verdict does not change the user's risk level in Entra. Purview Insider Risk covers data-exfiltration patterns from internal users — a different problem domain.

questions.question: A helpdesk operator needs to be able to elevate to the Global Administrator role only when an incident requires it. Each elevation must require approval, MFA, justification, and end automatically after one hour. Which Microsoft Entra Privileged Identity Management setup meets the requirement?
options: Permanently assign Global Administrator and require MFA at sign-in via a Conditional Access policy targeting the role
Make the operator eligible for Global Administrator in PIM, with activation requiring MFA, approval, justification, and a maximum activation duration of 1 hour
Add the operator to the Global Administrators group and set a one-hour session token lifetime in Conditional Access
Assign Global Administrator as an active assignment in PIM and review the audit log weekly for misuse
questions.explanation: PIM eligible role assignments grant Just-in-Time elevation, and the role's activation settings let you require MFA, approval, justification/ticket information, and a maximum activation duration (up to 24 hours). Permanent assignment leaves standing privilege — exactly what PIM exists to remove. Token lifetime controls a Conditional Access session, not the directory role assignment, so the operator would still be Global Admin once the token refreshed. An active PIM assignment also leaves the role permanently held; relying on after-the-fact audits is detective, not preventative.

questions.question: Membership of the "Finance-Reports" Microsoft Entra security group must be recertified quarterly by each member's manager. Any member whose manager fails to respond within the review period must be removed automatically. Which Microsoft Entra feature should you configure?
options: Conditional Access app control with session policies on the SharePoint sites
Entitlement Management access packages bundling the group with a quarterly policy
Access Reviews on the group with reviewer set to "Managers" and the "Remove access" default applied when reviewers don't respond
Microsoft Purview Data Loss Prevention with a Finance policy and access remediation actions
questions.explanation: Access Reviews can target a security or Microsoft 365 group, schedule a recurring quarterly review, pick "Managers" as the reviewer scope, and apply "Remove access" as the result when no decision is recorded — exactly the requirement. Conditional Access app control inspects session traffic; it does not recertify group membership. Entitlement Management governs broader resource bundles and is overkill for a single group. Purview DLP protects data being shared; it does not manage group membership.

questions.question: You are registering a single-page application written in React that signs users in with Microsoft Entra and calls Microsoft Graph. Per Microsoft's current guidance, no client secret may be stored in the browser. Which platform configuration and OAuth flow should you select for the app registration?
options: Web platform, client secret stored in Azure Key Vault, authorization code flow with client_credentials
Single-page application platform with redirect URI, authorization code flow with PKCE
Mobile and desktop applications (public client) platform with the device code flow
Web platform with the implicit grant flow returning both ID and access tokens in the URL fragment
questions.explanation: Modern browser SPAs register the Single-page application platform and use the authorization code flow with PKCE: no client secret is required, refresh tokens are issued with sender-constrained limits, and tokens never travel in the URL fragment. The Web platform requires a confidential client (a secret) — browsers cannot safely hold one. The Mobile and desktop public client platform with device code flow is for headless/CLI scenarios, not in-browser apps. The implicit grant flow is deprecated by Microsoft for new applications and exposes tokens in the URL.

questions.question: A company runs Active Directory Domain Services on-premises and wants users to sign in to Microsoft 365 with their existing AD password. Password hashes must NOT be stored in the cloud, and disabling an on-prem account must block Microsoft 365 sign-in within seconds. Which Microsoft Entra hybrid identity option meets these requirements with the least infrastructure?
options: Password Hash Synchronization with Entra Connect, plus Conditional Access requiring compliant devices
Pass-through Authentication with one or more Entra Connect agents, plus seamless single sign-on
Active Directory Federation Services with the Web Application Proxy in a perimeter network
Cloud-only accounts provisioned by Microsoft Graph PowerShell using the on-prem password as the initial value
questions.explanation: Pass-through Authentication validates each sign-in against on-prem AD via lightweight Connect Authentication Agents — no password hash leaves the directory, and disabling the AD account causes the next sign-in to fail immediately. Seamless SSO complements it. PHS synchronises the password hash to Entra, which the requirement forbids. AD FS satisfies the same constraints but requires deploying federation servers and the Web Application Proxy — more infrastructure than PTA. Cloud-only accounts are not synchronised, so disabling the on-prem user has no effect on the Microsoft 365 sign-in.

questions.question: An Azure Function must read secrets from Azure Key Vault during execution. No credentials may be stored in the Function app settings or repository. Which identity should the Function use to obtain a token, and what should you grant on the vault?
options: A service principal authenticated with a client certificate stored as a Function app setting; grant the principal Key Vault Secrets User
A system-assigned managed identity on the Function app; grant the identity Key Vault Secrets User via Azure RBAC on the vault
The deploying engineer's user account, granted Key Vault Secrets User at the resource group scope
A shared access signature token generated against the Key Vault, stored as a Function app setting
questions.explanation: Enabling a system-assigned managed identity on the Function app issues an Entra identity whose lifecycle is tied to the resource; the Function calls the IMDS endpoint to obtain a token and authenticates to Key Vault with the Secrets User role granted on the vault. No credentials are stored anywhere. A service principal with a certificate still requires the credential to be stored and rotated. The engineer's account is a human identity — it leaves when they do, and it grants production access via a personal credential. Key Vault does not issue SAS tokens (SAS is a storage construct, not a Key Vault one).

questions.question: Internal employees must be able to request a bundle that grants membership in a Teams team, a SharePoint site, and three line-of-business apps. The request must be approved by the resource owner, the assignment must expire after 180 days, and a recertification must run before renewal. Which Microsoft Entra feature should you configure?
options: Access Reviews configured separately on each of the five resources
Privileged Access Groups with Privileged Identity Management activation on the group
Entitlement Management access packages with an assignment policy, approval workflow, expiration, and an attached access review
Microsoft Purview Insider Risk Management policy with adaptive protection on the resources
questions.explanation: Entitlement Management access packages bundle multiple resources (security/Microsoft 365 groups, Teams, SharePoint Online sites, and Entra-integrated apps) and let you configure who can request, who approves, expiration, and an attached access review for renewal — exactly the scenario. Access Reviews recertify existing access; they do not grant or bundle new resources. Privileged Access Groups apply PIM activation to directory or Azure role assignments, not to user resource provisioning. Insider Risk Management detects risky data behaviour; it does not provision access.
